newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati left off parliamentary roll.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati left off parliamentary roll.

text.p: Indonesia's opposition figurehead Megawati Sukarnoputri was left out in the cold on Monday when the country's three recognised parties submitted candidates for next year's general elections.
Megawati, daughter of Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno, was ousted as leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) by a government-backed faction in June.
She was not on the list of PDI candidates submitted by new PDI leader Surjadi, the deputy speaker of parliament, at an official ceremony.

The Christian-nationalist PDI put forward 903 candidates for the elections to the 500-seat national assembly due to be held in June next year. Voters elect 425 members and the armed forces, whose members do not vote, appoint the remainder.
The ruling Golkar and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) each submitted 850 candidates.
Home Affairs Minister Yogie Memed said there were 124,740,978 registered voters out of a population of 196,286,613.
